source.title: DepthBench: Measuring How Residual Connections Enable More Computational Depth
source.authors: Ke-Yu Wang; Yang-Yi Huang; Jia-Le Kang; David González-Martínez; Wei-Yang Liu; Shi-Wei Liu

record.tranche_reason: The study varies width–depth shape at approximately fixed parameter and training budgets and measures held-out loss, directly examining whether architecture shape has little effect, though it does not reproduce the original scaling-law fits.
record.gate_note: The study does not fit power laws in parameters, tokens, or compute; test small-run extrapolation; or compare parameter–token allocations at fixed compute. Its downstream NLL evaluations compare shapes at a fixed model scale, not downstream performance as a function of scale or pretraining loss. Cited scaling-law results are not this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study varies width–depth aspect ratio (9.1–76.0, plus 6.5–78 in the iso-backbone control) at roughly fixed parameters and tokens. It measures held-out loss across 10 residual and normalization designs, which directly probes V4 by a method different from Kaplan's.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that the benefit of shifting capacity to depth at fixed parameters depends on architecture. HC and Full AttnRes keep improving at deep–narrow shapes, while Pre-LN and most normalization variants gain little or degrade. The gains go with more heterogeneous, order-sensitive layer computation. The authors identify hidden costs in mHC and Block AttnRes, and note that deeper shapes cost more compute and memory.
record.recipe_differences: This is a controlled width–depth allocation benchmark, not a fit of the original parameter/data/compute scaling laws. It trains models from scratch with a shared recipe and approximately fixed parameter budgets while varying aspect ratio and architecture.
record.method_sensitivity: Architecture changes the width–depth results. HC's trend is less stable across scale and may require finer learning-rate tuning. The paper also states that learning rate affects representation analyses and that LNS needs a substantially larger optimal learning rate than most variants.

fits_no_version.finding: At L=32, late-layer causal and permutation sensitivity is much higher for Full AttnRes (16%/46%) and HC (7%/35%) than for Pre-LN (1%/8%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Residual architecture affects how much late layers contribute non-interchangeable computation.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed parameters, going from aspect ratio 76 to 9.1 raises prefill FLOPs from about 3.0 to 4.4 TFLOPs per sequence and more than doubles KV cache.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At iso-parameter count, deeper shapes raise inference compute and memory, so iso-parameter shape comparisons are not iso-compute.

record.problems: The main validation-loss and domain-NLL comparisons do not report uncertainty in the text. Several exact per-shape results are presented only in figures. HC shows scale-dependent instability, including gradient explosion at one 500M setting, and the authors note it may need finer learning-rate tuning.
record.rows_left_out: Individual plotted values in Figures 2–4 are not transcribed where the text does not state them. The layerwise angular-distance, pruning, and LogitLens analyses are not catalogued as rows because they do not measure a listed claim version; late-layer causal and permutation measurements are included under fits_no_version.

untested.parts: No power-law fits of loss in parameters, tokens or compute.
No compute-optimal sweep. The study uses Chinchilla's 20 tokens/parameter as its recipe without testing it.
Only width–depth ratio is varied. Head count, FFN ratio and other shape details are not varied. Shapes are run only at about 20 tokens per parameter.
Domain NLL is compared across shapes at fixed scale, not as a function of scale or pretraining loss.
Exponents and fitting choices are not examined.

missing.what: Iso-backbone 300M control: Pre-LN, HC and Full AttnRes across aspect ratios 6.48–78. Deep–narrow HC and Full AttnRes improve even as total size falls.
Extended fixed-400M range to L=70 (aspect ratio 9.1) for Pre-LN, HC and Full AttnRes.
Per-scale Pre-LN results across 200M–500M and 1.6B: Pre-LN is plotted but has no row.
Learning-rate sweeps per shape. The authors say the optimal learning rate is consistent across shapes within each architecture.

record.verdict_notes: The reader coded row states against 'depth helps' rather than V4's 'shape matters little', which inverted most states. Its 'challenges' label is not supported: the largest reported shape effect is about 1.2% of loss, within the 'few percent' range Kaplan described. I gave limits_scope for the consistent, architecture-dependent direction instead. The authors' framing emphasises shape effects more than the magnitudes do. No uncertainty is reported for the loss comparisons, and the differences are about 0.03 nats from single runs. Tranche could arguably be T5, but the study frames no argument against V4 itself.

versions.untested_parts: No power-law fits across parameter count, training tokens, or compute.
No small-run fits or predictions of much larger runs.
No sweep of loss-minimising parameter and token counts across compute budgets.
Tests width–depth aspect-ratio allocation across residual and normalization designs under approximately fixed parameter budgets; does not systematically vary every other architectural detail.
Text-only pretraining; no other modalities, repeated-data regimes, fine-tuning, or transfer scaling laws.
Downstream NLL is measured across shapes at a fixed model scale, not as a function of scale or pretraining loss.
Does not compare fitted exponents or compute-optimal splits under different fitting choices; learning-rate sensitivity is examined but does not test those fits.

relationships.reason: Shape still moves loss only ~1%, but consistently and monotonically toward depth, so the optimal shape depends on residual design. Deeper shapes also raise FLOPs and memory at fixed parameters (r7, r8, r11–r13).

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: The quantified 400M comparisons show small loss changes compatible with V4, even though preferences are systematic. V4 promises neither constant compute nor constant memory. Other scales provide qualitative preferences without establishing large loss changes, and HC explicitly lacks the same clear depth improvement at 1.6B; this condition group must be narrowed.

relation.reason: The study reports its own approximately parameter-matched shape sweeps and held-out loss measurements bearing on V4.

tranche.reason: The controlled comparison of residual designs and width–depth allocations directly tests architecture sensitivity of held-out pretraining loss.

source_check.notes: Extreme-shape curves in Figure 2(b–c) cover Pre-LN, HC and Full AttnRes; the blanket full-range percentage bound is unsupported. Reported bootstrap uncertainty concerns residual-transport diagnostics, not repeated-training uncertainty for the loss sweeps; the paper also announces released code despite code=n in the pack.

statements.correction: Full AttnRes: 2.751 at L=16, 2.718 at L=32. HC: 2.729 at L=16, 2.699 at L=32. Small, systematic loss changes; V4 does not require shape preferences to be absent.
statements.problem: The DepthBench numbers and systematic preferences are correct, but their small magnitude does not itself justify the limits_scope label for V4.
